name: Shielding across period 2
description: Watch the 2p orbital shrink as effective nuclear charge grows from boron to fluorine. Same orbital, same shielding electrons — only the proton count changes.

steps.caption: Boron (Z = 5), 2p orbital. The two inner 1s electrons screen most of the nucleus, so this outer electron feels an effective charge of only about 2.6. The cloud sits comparatively far from the nucleus.
Carbon (Z = 6), 2p orbital. We added one proton but the shielding is almost unchanged, so Z_eff jumps to about 3.25. The cloud pulls noticeably tighter — already smaller than boron's.
Nitrogen (Z = 7), 2p orbital. Z_eff is now around 3.9. Each new proton tugs the cloud inward more than the new same-shell electron pushes it out, because same-shell partners are weak screeners.
Oxygen (Z = 8), 2p orbital. Z_eff is roughly 4.55 — the orbital is now markedly compact compared to boron's. This monotonic contraction across a period is why atomic radii shrink left-to-right.

Fluorine (Z = 9), 2p orbital. With Z_eff near 5.2 the cloud is at its tightest in this tour. Fluorine's small, hard-pulled valence electrons are exactly why it's the most electronegative element of all.
